main_concerns.concern: The planned 'feedback packet' that summarizes tester artifacts for the developer is an un-specified summarization step. Unless it is a lossless, structured artifact, the runner will reinterpret or compress the failure signal, which can quietly downgrade validation and turn the tester from a strict failure reporter into an indirect, diluted guidance source.

Prompt-level enforcement of hard-failure semantics is insufficient for the observed failure mode. The developer already produced warnings instead of hard failures under existing prompts; adding more prompt text does not guarantee behavioral change. A code-level post-developer scan that programmatically rejects outputs with warning severity on critical categories (remote-dependency, signup-empty, file-protocol) must gate developer output before tester invocation, otherwise the bounded loop risks being a bounded waste of rounds with no behavioral difference between iterations.

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Before coding, require a lossless feedback packet schema (derived deterministically from tester artifacts, no suggested fixes) and a loop invariant that tracks the failure set across rounds: stop with final failure if the fixed cap is reached, if no failure from the prior round is eliminated, or if a previously fixed failure reappears.

Add a programmatic post-developer severity gate before the repair loop begins: after each developer invocation, scan the output for warning-level severity on the critical categories (remote-dependency, signup-empty, file-protocol). If any warning is found, reject the developer output immediately and record it as a pre-tester failure with the specific warnings enumerated. This gate must run in code (not prompts) and must increment the repair round counter. Only developer outputs that pass this gate proceed to tester. Without this, the loop is structurally identical to re-running the current pipeline N times and hoping for a different result.
